successors.name: Republic of India
successors.text: Tehri Garhwal: the Tehri Garhwal district and most of Uttarkashi district

ledger.x: 823: the Garhwal Kingdom is founded at Chandpur Garhi.
1358: Ajay Pal unifies the principalities of Garhwal.
14 May 1804: Pradyumna Shah is defeated and killed by the Gurkhas at Khurbura near Dehradun and Garhwal passes to them.
1815: the Gorkhas are driven out of Garhwal and Tehri Garhwal is restored under the British.
ledger.cpn: British Empire in India (East India Company rule)

ledger.x: August 1949: Tehri Garhwal accedes to the Union of India.

wars.name: Rohilla invasion of the Dun
wars.outcome: Najib-ud-daula captured Dehradun in 1757; Garhwali forces retook the Dun in 1770.

wars.name: Gorkha conquest of Garhwal
wars.outcome: Pradyumna Shah was defeated at the Battle of Khurbura near Dehradun and died on 14 May 1804; the Gorkhas merged Garhwal into Nepal in 1804 (infobox) and held it to 1814 (1815 on the Sugauli page).

wars.name: Anglo-Nepalese War
wars.outcome: Ochterlony pushed the Nepalese out of Garhwal and Kumaon in 1815; the Treaty of Sugauli, signed 4 March 1816, made the Kali the western boundary and the British annexed half of Garhwal (Pauri Garhwal) and restored the other half as Tehri Garhwal.

certainty.note: The page gives no boundary; the principalities and the Dun are regions.
The treaty division of 1815 and the princely state of Tehri Garhwal (10,800 km2 in 1901) are named administrative units; the drawn circles are approximate.
